name: Ceramics Engineering
boundaries: Ceramics Engineering: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: Intrinsic room-temperature ductility in bulk structural ceramics
original_dispositions.reason: The paired demands of more than 10 percent elongation and hardness above 30 GPa were not adopted.

original_dispositions.original_title: Autonomous, multi-cycle self-healing under load at high temperature
original_dispositions.reason: The entry is wider than the 1000–2000 °C oxidation case, and it includes that case.

original_dispositions.original_title: Perfectly transparent polycrystalline ceramics with theoretical strength
original_dispositions.reason: Not merged into CRM-01. Transparency at a few hundred megapascals already exists. The open principle is near-theoretical strength in a thick optical section. Overlap with CRM-01 is flagged.
Sodium is the same barrier, not a new identifier. The figure above 10⁻² S/cm was not adopted as a standard.

original_dispositions.original_title: Ambient-pressure ceramic superconductor “>77 K” with high current density
original_dispositions.reason: Ambient-pressure cuprates already exceeded 77 K decades ago. The Deng et al. 2026 abstract describes an ambient-pressure record plateau since 1993 that the new 151 K result only then moved, still about 122 degrees below 0 °C. The open problem is room temperature plus useful polycrystalline current. A separate “>77 K” entry would describe an achieved breakthrough.

original_dispositions.original_title: Ultra-high-temperature ceramics with oxidation resistance above 3000 °C
original_dispositions.reason: The silica limit near 1700 °C, documented by Kane et al., is the evidenced barrier. The 3000 °C figure was not adopted. It is not a separate concept.

original_dispositions.original_title: Zero-shrinkage, crack-free additive manufacturing of fully dense technical ceramics
original_dispositions.reason: Narrowed so that “zero” means no machining of functional surfaces, and so that silica ornaments and still-shrinking zirconia do not count. Overlap with CRM-04 is flagged.

The percentage is not a defined metric. BiFeO3 is already a room-temperature multiferroic. The remaining device-materials problem was not judged a missing principle on the scale of the calibration examples.

original_dispositions.original_title: Perfect osseointegration and full regeneration of load-bearing bone
original_dispositions.reason: Bioactive ceramics that bond to bone already exist. Critical-size defects are still clinically unsolved, and the remaining barriers are not a single ceramic discovery. Load-bearing brittleness, where it is the ceramic limit, is the territory of CRM-01.

original_dispositions.original_title: Programmable shape-memory or morphing ceramics with more than 5 percent recoverable strain
original_dispositions.reason: The strain figure is that list’s proposal. High-temperature solid-state motion would be useful, but it extends an existing actuator class and was not judged to open a new general capability on the scale of the calibration examples.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Preserved CRM-01 through CRM-10 and their identities. No first-pass concept was deleted or replaced.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The first-pass concepts stay in place.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Clarified that the historical elongation and hardness figures are not criteria. Flagged CRM-12 as a different mechanism with an overlapping reliability consequence.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Ductility and flaw elimination are different mechanisms.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Clarified that “above 3000 °C” is the same oxidation problem, not a new concept, and is not the completion criterion.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The Kane threshold above 1700 °C remains the evidenced barrier.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Clarified that room-temperature sodium ceramics are the same superionic problem. Did not adopt 10⁻² S/cm as a standard.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The same ionic barrier applies to a room-temperature sodium ceramic.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Flagged overlap with new CRM-11 without merging.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Cold densification and net-shape printing solve different constraints.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Corrected the coating-review DOI from an unverified string to 10.1016/j.ceramint.2025.09.272, with authors Lgaz, Lee, and Messali. Added the 2025 oxidation-healing review and the 2025 MAX nanowire result. Stated that the historical high-temperature case is included, not the whole scope.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Nanoscale room-temperature healing should not be mistaken for bulk structural healing.
Ambient-pressure cuprates already passed it. The open claim remains room temperature and polycrystalline current.
Sources from the first pass were reused where they had been inspected.

Structural ceramics still shrink on the order of 15–30 percent by volume or about 20 percent linearly when dense, while a January 2026 silica print shows that low shrinkage and full density can coincide for one oxide only.

Evidence: transparent AlON at 82.5 percent transmittance and 401 MPa bending strength, spinel still limited by contact brittleness, fracture stresses generally one to two orders below theoretical shear strength, and thin-specimen strengths that do not predict large components.
For the reasons in the disposition.
